Desktop Won't Power On

  1. Unplug power.
  2. Hold down power button for 10 seconds, press it a few more times.
  3. Open case.
  4. Remove all sticks of ram.
  5. Plug in power.
  6. Power on.
  7. If it beeps the computer is booting up to a point where it recognizes the ram is missing. This is good. If it does not beep you may have Power Supply or Motherboard Issues. Try a new Power supply of equal or greater wattage.
  8. Assuming it beeped, Power off the computer.
  9. Repeat steps 1 & 2.
  10. Re-insert all sticks of ram (or just one, your call) (If you suspect one of the sticks to be bad, only boot with one of them, later try with all).
  11. Power on.
  12. If it boots up like normal then you're all good. This whole process is called "Reseating the RAM", and is the most common fix for computers not powering on.

Laptop Won't Power On

  1. Unplug AC Adapter (power cord).
  2. Remove battery.
  3. Hold down power button for 10 seconds, press it a few more times.
  4. Plug in AC Adapter (without battery).
  5. Power on.
  6. If it does not boot up like normal proceed to Step 7. If it does boot up normally:
    • Shut it down..
    • Unplug power.
    • Hold power button for 10 seconds.
    • Put the battery back in.
    • Plug in the power cord.
    • Turn it back on. You've successfully "Reseated the Battery".
  7. Repeat steps 1, 2, and 3.
  8. Locate and remove all sticks of RAM from the computer.
  9. Repeat step 4 and 5.
  10. If it beeps the computer is booting up to a point where it recognizes the ram is missing. This is good. If it does not beep you may have a Motherboard issue. Paying someone to replace the motherboard isn't cost effective. Remove the hard drive, place it in a cheap hard drive enclosure to make it an external hard drive, and find a new computer.
  11. Assuming it beeped, power off the computer.
  12. Repeat step 1, 2, and 3.
  13. Reinsert all or just one of the sticks of RAM (your call) (If you suspect one of the sticks to be bad, only boot with one of them, later try with all).
  14. Plug in AC Adapter (power cord).
  15. Power on.
  16. If it boots up normally then shut it down, unplug power, insert battery, plug power back in. You've just "Reseated the RAM". This is the most common solution for computers not powering on.

Graphics Card/Video Card Driver Issues

  1. A common fix is updating the drivers for you gfx card. If you have a retail/store bought computer (like a Dell, HP, Sony, Toshiba, etc), go to the manufacture's website. If you have a homebuilt PC skip to step 7.
  2. On their site, find the Support & Downloads section. There should be a link to either a drivers section of a download section.
  3. At some point it will ask you to either type in your computer's Serial Number/Product Number/Service Tag, or it will ask for the model number. Both should be available on the surface of your computer.
  4. After entering in the information you'll be taken to a page with all the downloads for that computer, look through what is available, ignore the downloads that are obviously not video card related. In most cases there is only one download option. If there are multiples and you are not sure, post your computer specs in a in the subreddit by clicking this link and filling out the form provided.
  5. After locating the correct driver, download the version for your version of windows and instal the new driver software. Reboot the computer after install.
  6. If issues persist create a post in the subreddit explaining the issues and what you have attempted thus far.
  7. If you have a home built PC, use a hardware inventory tool like Speccy, System Information for Windows (SIW), or HWiNFO32 to find out what kind of card you have.
  8. Go to the manufacturer of the card's website, find their Drivers & Support section.
  9. Do a search for the type of card you have, or if they have an option to detect the card, use that (usually quicker and more accurate, but if it gives obviously wrong results, look it up manually).
  10. Download and install the driver for your version of Windows. After installed, reboot.
  11. If issue persists post system spec information in the subreddit.

Graphics Card/Video Card Testing

  1. Sadly there's very little in the area of free diagnostic tools for graphics cards. If you're lucky there will be some available from the card manufacturer, but this is rare. So we'll cover 3 things that you can use as quick tests.
  2. First, the easiest test, and it's built in to windows. On XP Click start and go to run and type in DXDIAG and hit ok. On Vista/7/8, click start and type in DXDIAG and hit enter.
  3. Look through the tabs and run any tests that are available, see if it gives you any errors.
  4. Download GPU-Z, it's free and available as a portable app from LiberKey.
  5. Run GPU-Z, it will monitor your cards performace.
  6. Download GPU Caps Viewer, it's free and available as a portable app from LiberKey.
  7. With GPU-Z still running, open GPU Caps Viewer, at the bottom of the program are two dropdown lists, you can try running those tests at low resolutions, then at high resolutions. Some tests may not be available for your card.
  8. If you see any visual glitching there may be an issue with the card itself or just the driver. If the tests run fine, you're probably okay. You can find one that stresses your card, set it to a high anti-alias and high resolution (try around 90% of your screen resolution), let it run for a while to see if it over heats.

RAM Diagnostics

  1. Download and burn HBCD to a disc
  2. Pop in the disc and boot to it
    • You may need to press an F-Key (F1-F12) or DEL or ESC on boot to choose the boot order so the CD/DVD Drive boots.
  3. Choose MemTest 86
  4. This will run several different tests, when all tests complete it will say you have completed 1 Pass.
  5. Let it run 2-10 passes. Sometimes brand new RAM won't show any faults in the first few passes.
    • 10 passes is excessive. If there are no issues found by the 10th pass there's no reason to let it keep going. Hit ESC, eject the disc and reboot.
    • If the RAM fails the test continue to step 6.
  6. Shutdown the computer, unplug power, hold down power button for 10 seconds.
  7. Remove all RAM except one stick. Run diags one stick at a time to see which are good and which are bad. Replace bad RAM with a new stick.
    • Note: Some motherboards require matching pairs of RAM to run. You may need to run two sticks at a time in this case.
  8. If you need to purchase new RAM and you don't know what type, look up your Computer's model on sites like Crucial, Kingston, or PNY. These are all RAM manufacturers, purchasing RAM directly from them is typically more expensive than finding it on sites like Newegg, TigerDirect, or Amazon.

CPU Stress Tests

One of the easiest ways to stress test a CPU is to download Prime95. Run it in Windows, it will max out your CPU. If you suspect that your CPU is overheating, maxing it out for a few minutes (10-30) is a quick test. The computer will blue screen or shut off if the CPU temp gets too high. Or just throttle itself back until it cools down. If it's overheating, get a can of compressed air and spray out the inside of the computer, especially the fans while it's turned off.

I don't know if I can take these disaster preparedness tests seriously.

When I was in the military we used to do something called "fight the base." It was a week where we'd split the entire base in half and pray war games. Half would attack the base, and the other half would defend it.

Overall, it was fun, but the purpose was to determine where our strategic weak points were and address them before we had to implement them in the real world.

Well, one night, I went to a captain and asked why we were doing a specific thing a specific way. I pointed out that it would be less taxing, and more efficient to do it a different way with different people.

He agreed wholeheartedly, but told me it wasn't going to change. When I pointed out the purpose of the exercise, and asked him why we weren't going to suggest the change, he told me (and I'll never forget it), "Well, that's how we've always done it."

That's when I realized we weren't fighting a war against AL Qaeda, or a war on terror, or even a proxy war for oil... We were fighting common sense.
